prompt: A change broke checkout in production, so the team undoes that commit with a new commit.
tells: undoes that commit with a new commit
why: Instead of erasing the bad commit, the team adds a new commit that does the opposite. That's git revert.
trap: A flag would switch off without a new commit.

prompt: The fastest fix is to back out yesterday's change and investigate later.
why: Undoing the change first stops the damage; working out the cause can wait. Backing out a change is a revert.

prompt: A bad merge is reversed without rewriting shared history.
why: Rewriting history others already have breaks their copies, so the bad merge is undone with a new commit instead. That's revert.
trap: The merge is done, so there's no conflict left to resolve.

prompt: git revert a1b2c3 creates a change that cancels an earlier one.
why: git revert makes a new commit that cancels the changes of an earlier one. The old commit stays in history.
trap: It is a commit, but its job is undoing.

prompt: The team rolls back to the last good version while they look for the cause.
tells: rolls back to the last good version
why: Going back to the last version that worked stops the problem while the cause is found. Rolling back like this is a revert.

prompt: She undoes a pushed commit safely, so teammates' copies aren't broken.
why: Revert adds a commit rather than removing one, so teammates who already pulled aren't left with broken history.
trap: Deleting history would break their copies.
